items.title: Etaleness of a base-changed algebra map is realised at a finite stage of the colimit
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if a base-changed map of algebras is etale and the source is of finite presentation, then the base-changed map is already etale at some single stage of the colimit (statement lines 47842-47854). The proof does not invoke a general descent theorem for etale maps: it writes explicit presentations, records the differential isomorphism that etaleness amounts to, and then uses that tensor products commute with directed colimits to bring the finitely many witnessing elements, and the relations they satisfy, down to one stage (proof lines 47856-47880). Recognising the hypothesis as finitely many equations, so that it can be descended, is the content of the argument. H2.
